newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwait sees oil prices stable after Iraqi return.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sees oil prices stable after Iraqi return.

text.p: Kuwait Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said on Saturday that he believed oil prices would remain stable despite Iraq's limited return to the oil market under a United Nations oil-for-food deal.

"We believe that prices will stay the same," he told reporters at an Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries' (OAPEC) meeting in Cairo when asked for his reaction to Iraq's return to the oil market after six years.
Iraq resumed limited exports of oil on December 10 for the first time since sanctions were imposed on Iraq shortly after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Benchmark Brent blend fell after news that Iraqi crude had begun to flow through the trans-Turkey pipeline under the U.N. plan which allows Iraq to buy humanitarian supplies. It ended at $23.55 a barrel with a $1.00 per barrel rally on Friday.
OAPEC groups Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Country (OPEC) members Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Libya, Algeria, United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Iraq with non-OPEC producers Bahrain, Syria and Egypt.
Unlike OPEC the OAPEC does not set production levels.

Delegates described the OAPEC meeting as officially an economic one in which they discussed mutual projects. A statement said they set the OAPEC general secretariat budget for 1997 of 1.39 million Kuwaiti dinars ($4.65 million).

Asked if Kuwait would change its output level of two million barrels per day supposing prices fell, Mazeedi said: "I cannot suppose because this is the fact, it (prices) will not. Do not give me any assumptions.
"We are restricting ourselves, so is everybody else in the OPEC organisation, to really produce as their share of the quotas."
Mazeedi said a strong world economy and the advent of the northern winter were among reasons why he thought prices would remain stable.

"As we have mentioned before we don't believe and neither does any of the OPEC members believe that Iraq entering the world market would affect neither the prices nor really the ceiling of the OPEC..." he said.

"First of all the world economy is very strong...and also the strong economy of the industrial world is rising, so these are very strongly indicative as to the stability of the prices for some time in the future," Mazeedi said.
"Add to that, that still the world stock is a little bit under the level that it should be. Fourth we are just about to start the winter," he added.
